title: Public ShakeAlert contours for 439 earthquakes (2019-2026) matched station shaking counts only because high magnitudes offset a lookup that predicts too little intensity below M5
abstract: Question: Do the public USGS ShakeAlert earthquake early warning MMI contours predict the observed shaking area without bias, and which part of the error comes from the source estimate and which from the contour lookup? Approach: We wrote a plan before we downloaded outcome data. We parsed all 522 ShakeAlert summary products in ComCat (2019-2026) and compared their MMI 2.5, 3.5 and 4.5 contours with instrumental intensity at 121,308 seismic-station records (439 public-alert-era events), with the product's own GMICE (Worden 2012 eq. 3+10), and with 743,181 DYFI responses. We recovered the contour lookup r(edge, M) from 2,776 published polygons and built counterfactual contours with the ShakeAlert and the ANSS (true) source. Results: The reconstructed published contours were approximately unbiased in station count (frequency bias B = 1.11 [0.91, 1.31] at MMI 2.5; 1.24 [0.82, 1.71] at 3.5). With the true magnitude and epicentre, the same lookup covered only about 60% of the stations that reached each edge (B = 0.59, 0.61, 0.62), and 16-50% below M4.5. Observed minus lookup intensity was +0.6 to +1.1 MMI units at 10-160 km for M < 5 and down to -0.8 for M >= 5.5 far away. Site condition explained little. Peak ShakeAlert magnitudes were high by about 0.3 units for M3.5-5, which enlarged the contours 2.0-2.6 times and cancelled the deficit in aggregate. The cancellation was not uniform: B = 0.47 for M < 4 and 2.1 for M5.0-5.5 at MMI 2.5. Location error had almost no effect. For phone-app alerts, 58% of stations with MMI >= 2.5 were alerted before the S wave, 16% late and 26% not alerted. At MMI >= 4.5, 40% were alerted in time and 60% late (13% in time with 5 s delivery delay). An exploratory magnitude-dependent offset fitted on 2019-2022 increased the MMI 3.5 success ratio from 0.31 to 0.53 and the detection probability from 0.62 to 0.73 on 258 events in 2023-2026. Implication: better ShakeAlert magnitudes without a lookup update would make alert areas for M < 5 events about half of the shaken area. Limitations: the GMICE defines the MMI truth; the public summaries omit or cut some contours, which we reconstructed; peak-alert times are upper bounds; M >= 5.5 has only 11-12 events.

display.caption: Frequency bias B (stations inside contour / stations with observed MMI at or above the edge) by ANSS magnitude for the reconstructed published product (blue), the recovered lookup at the ShakeAlert source (orange) and the lookup at the true ANSS source (green). The true-source lookup is too small below M5; magnitude overestimates enlarge the operational contours. 95% event-bootstrap intervals; log scale.

Mean observed station MMI minus contour-lookup MMI by distance and ANSS magnitude, with the true source (left) and the ShakeAlert effective source (right). Stations selected on the prediction only (lookup MMI >= 1.5).

Alert outcome at seismic stations that reached MMI 2.5, 3.5 or 4.5, for the phone channel (M >= 4.5, MMI 2.5 contour) and the WEA channel (M >= 5, MMI 3.5 contour). Alert time is the initial alert if the site was inside the initial contour, else the peak-alert time (upper bound); S arrival at 3.5 km/s.
